challenges.title: Selfie Evidence
challenges.description:
A "proof of attendance" photo was posted in the club group chat. It was taken on a phone that still tags everything.

No pixel analysis required — the file knows more than the photographer.

**Goal:** read the metadata and submit the flag. The flag sits verbatim in the `UserComment` tag; the GPS coordinates only tell you where the photo was taken — they are not part of the flag and nothing is hidden at that location.

hints.text: `exiftool attendance.jpg` is the whole beginning and end of this challenge.
Look for GPSLatitude, GPSLongitude and UserComment.

challenges.title: Deleted but Not Gone
challenges.description:
A 4 MB disk image from a club laptop. The previous owner deleted a text file, emptied the trash, and called it a day.

On FAT32, deleting a file only clears the directory entry. The clusters are still there until something overwrites them.

**Goal:** carve the deleted file and read it.

hints.text: Try `strings` first, then `binwalk -e`, then a real carving tool.
The file signature you are looking for is plain ASCII text at the start of a cluster.

challenges.title: Broken ZIP
challenges.description:
The archive downloaded from the club drive will not extract. The download script overwrote the first four bytes, which now read `FF D8 FF E0` — the start of a JPEG, not a ZIP.

The central directory is untouched, so `unzip -l` still lists the two members — but extraction of the first one is refused: `bad zipfile offset (local header sig)` from `unzip`, `zipfile.BadZipFile: Bad magic number for file header` from Python.

**Goal:** restore the four magic bytes and extract the flag.

hints.text: A ZIP local file header starts with `PK\x03\x04`.
Patch those four bytes only — `printf 'PK\003\004' | dd of=evidence.zip bs=1 seek=0 conv=notrunc`. The central directory is fine, so no rebuild is needed.

challenges.title: Memory Lane
challenges.description:
A workstation was imaged after a suspected intrusion. The disk was clean; the RAM was not.

**Goal:** identify the suspicious process, dump its memory region, and recover the flag the operator typed into it.

hints.text: Start with `vol -f workstation.raw windows.pslist` and look for a process with no parent.

challenges.title: Timeline Tangle
challenges.description:
Three log sources, three timezones, one incident. The web server logs in UTC, the firewall in local Tunis time, and the VPN in whatever the vendor felt like.

**Goal:** build a single timeline and identify the exact second the attacker moved laterally — the first SMB connection coming from a VPN-assigned address.

Submit that moment in ISO-8601 UTC: `SNT{YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ}`.

hints.text: Tunisia is UTC+1 all year — no daylight saving since 2008.
The lateral movement is the first successful SMB connection from a VPN-assigned address.

challenges.title: Ransom Notes
challenges.description:
A ransomware sample was recovered from a quarantined endpoint. It is packed, but the packer is lazy and the decryption routine is a single-byte XOR over an embedded blob.

**Goal:** statically recover the configuration — including the flag used as the campaign ID — without executing the sample.

hints.text: Find high-entropy regions, then look for a short loop that XORs a buffer in place.
The key is derived from the first four bytes of the resource section. Brute force all 255 single-byte keys and grep for `SNT{`.
